chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari narrated from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad — all from Ibn Faddal, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying — and he mentioned the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) — then he said: 'O Allah! Indeed You know that he is more beloved to us than fathers, mothers, and cold water.'

key_terms.أَحَبُّ: More beloved — comparative form expressing superlative love
key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ: O Allah — the vocative address in supplication, combining Allah with the emphatic suffix -umma
key_terms.الْمَاءُ الْبَارِدُ: Cold water — a classical Arabic expression for something most precious and refreshing, used to indicate the utmost degree of love

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about his love for the Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: Ubayd ibn Zurara, a direct companion of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), reports hearing the Imam invoke God's name while speaking of the Prophet (SAWW), expressing through supplication the depth of love the Imams and believers hold for the Prophet. The comparison to fathers, mothers, and cold water — three things universally dear to people — reflects an ancient Arabic rhetorical device for expressing the highest degree of love. Cold water in the desert context of Arabia was among the most prized comforts, making this comparison particularly evocative of the Prophet's supreme station.
